messages:
alex: FYI customer ACME reporting 403 on console invite flow after their Okta group merge. They say invites used to work, now 'You do not have permission' in project UI and Create invite API returns 403.

sara: Can you paste the API response + request id from the customer?

alex: Pasting minimal repro from their engineer:
```bash
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/orgs/org_1234/projects/proj_987/invites \n  -H 'Authorization: Bearer sk-live-XXX' \n  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \n  -d '{"email":"newuser@acme.com","role":"project.editor"}'
```
Response: 403
```json
{
  "error": {
    "code": "permission.denied",
    "message": "Invite blocked: user mapping not in allowed groups (shadowed by external service identity)",
    "request_id": "req_0a1b2c3d"
  }
}
```
They also attached a screenshot of the console with the top-right toast: "403: insufficient permissions".

matt: @jordan any known SCIM/claim mapping changes this week? Customer mentioned they merged two Okta groups that contained project-editor binding.

jordan: IDP team rolled a small normalization change in SCIM last night to dedupe group names and rewrite group display names (to handle whitespace). That change intentionally keeps canonical "group_id" stable, but there was a bug where we reissued new internal group_ids when external groups had identical names across orgs.

idp-bot: SCIM sync job job_782 started 2026-03-15T02:14:32Z, completed with warnings. 2 groups remapped, 1 generated new internal id. (see job_782 logs) :warning:

alex: Customer's timeline matches. After the Okta merge, the group's external id changed and our SCIM job created a new internal group and didn't migrate the role bindings -> resulting in no binding for the merged group. So invite API checks allowed_group_ids and failed.

sara: Quick reproduction steps for support/eng to validate locally: 1) create two groups with same display name in a test org; 2) run scim normalize/merge; 3) attempt to invite a user who belongs to external merged group but whose internal group_id has no binding. If we repro, we can craft a hotfix.

matt: Adding repro snippet for engineers:
```python
# simulate mapping table lookup failure
external_group = {'external_id': 'okta_abc', 'display_name': 'acme-editors'}
# SCIM created new internal id instead of migrating binding
internal_map = {'okta_old': 'g-111', 'okta_abc_new': 'g-999'}
# permission check uses internal_map[external_group.external_id] -> g-999 not bound to project
```

jordan: Temporary customer workaround: manually add the new internal group id to the project role or rebind the role to the external group via SCIM console. For ACME we can also manually add the user to project while we patch.

sara: @matt can you triage on-call priority? This is customer-facing and blocks invites.

matt: Yep picking up. Plan: revert the normalization that created new internal IDs and run a migration to remap role bindings to the canonical id. Prep hotfix branch and smoke tests. ETA for patch: ~2h.

deploy-bot: Deploy pipeline:hotfix/scim-group-migrate triggered by matt at 2026-03-15T09:10Z. Running tests.

alex: Customer accepted manual add workaround for now (they added the user via project owners). They asked for timeline and whether this will affect other orgs.

jordan: We'll run a scan across orgs for recent SCIM jobs that created new internal group ids and flag any with role bindings missing. If count > 0 we'll schedule backfill. Otherwise per-org fixes.

matt: Hotfix deployed to staging, backfill script ready. Deploying to prod in ~30m after a small safety window. Communicating with ACME after prod deploy.

alex: Thanks team. I'll update the customer with ETA and the manual workaround steps.

sara: After resolution we should add a guard in sync job to never create new internal ids when external group has an existing binding in the same org. Filing followup ticket: INF-2241. :white_check_mark:

jordan: Agreed. Also add an alert when SCIM job remaps >1 group_id per external id.

matt: Marking this as "investigating -> hotfix in progress". Will post final status when prod backfill completes.

deploy-bot: Prod deploy successful at 2026-03-15T09:54Z. Hotfix applied. Backfill started (job_backfill_55).

alex: Customer confirmed invites working again after prod fix. Closing the escalation once backfill finishes. :tada:
